findings.problem: The same step appears three times inline in this one proof: evaluate a convergent sequence of continuous linear maps at a fixed vector. Each copy builds `(ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).continuous.tendsto G`, composes it with `(hD*conv j).tendsto_at hj`, and restates the long `Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (… (φ (ψ n))) p v) …` type by hand. The sibling file FiniteContradictionClosure.lean has already factored this out as `tendsto_clm_apply_of_tendsto`. There the same hdiv/hWr skeleton on the half-plane uses it, and each limit shrinks to one line. So the receding file repeats machinery that exists as a named lemma, and the two copies of the argument can drift apart. This sits on top of the broader duplication of the two-stage extraction (obtain φ for V, re-extract ψ for W, compose, transport the V convergences along ψ) across the two files.
findings.proposed_change: Move `tendsto_clm_apply_of_tendsto` out of FiniteContradictionClosure.lean into a shared Analysis file that both closures import, for example next to `tendstoUniformlyOn_comp_strictMono` in ArzelaAscoliC1HalfPlane.lean or the plane variant. Its statement is `{F : ℕ → (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ} {G} (h : Tendsto F atTop (nhds G)) (v : ℝ × ℝ) : Tendsto (fun n => F n v) atTop (nhds (G v))`, and its proof is the existing one-liner `((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).continuous.tendsto G).comp h`. Then rewrite the receding uses. In `hdiv`, `have h1 := tendsto_clm_apply_of_tendsto ((hDVconv j).tendsto_at hj) (1, 0)` and `have h3 := tendsto_clm_apply_of_tendsto ((hDWconv j).tendsto_at hj) (0, 1)`. In `hWr`, `have h1 := tendsto_clm_apply_of_tendsto ((hDWconv j).tendsto_at hj) (1, 0)`. The `hdWn p` hypothesis at line 132 and the rest of both proofs stay unchanged. The hypotheses are unchanged. `(hDVconv j).tendsto_at hj` has type `Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (Vseq (φ (ψ n))) p) atTop (nhds (DV p))`, which is exactly the lemma's input with `F n = fderiv ℝ (Vseq (φ (ψ n))) p`. The elaborated types of h1, h2, h3 then match what `hev` and `congr'` already expect.
findings.benefit: The three type-annotated blocks of about four lines each become one-liners. The half-plane and plane closures share one named lemma instead of keeping two diverging inline versions of the same limit-through-evaluation step. Any later change to how the C¹ limits are used, such as a different convergence mode, is made in one place.
